rule.quote:
# TC10 — Commit and Push Every Task Completion and Handback

**Severity: HIGH — prevent lost work and divergent histories across concurrently
active agents and machines. Binding for every agent role and runtime.**

## 0. The rule

At each completed task and handback, review the task's artifacts, stage only its
changes, commit, immediately push through the configured HTTPS Forgejo origin,
and verify the push and remote commit reachability. A local-only commit is an
incomplete delivery. Unrelated dirty work is preserved; it does not excuse leaving
a completed task unpushed. Do not require repeated approval for this standing
instruction.

In a shared checkout, name one integrator to publish each worker's completed
handback promptly. Workers report exact files, verification, and gaps without
racing shared Git mutations. This coordinates the delivery obligation; it does
not defer it until the end of a multi-task project. Direct single-agent sessions
perform their own commit and push.

## 1. Why push has priority

The operator runs concurrent agents on multiple machines. A local commit protects
against some working-tree losses but remains invisible to the next machine; that
machine can continue from another ancestor and create divergent histories. Push
is part of task completion because prompt shared visibility prevents that failure.
Uncommitted changes also risk loss through cleanup, mistaken reset, or interrupted
handoff. A filesystem edit is durable on disk until changed or lost; compaction
alone does not delete it, but can lose the context needed to identify and recover
it. Commit plus verified publication preserves both content and provenance.

Apply SC3's “net of all” ranked multicriteria judgment. Short means this handback;
medium means the next task and concurrent sessions; long means recovery and future
maintenance. Assess every available fact, including inconsistent lineage, unknown
remote state, large historical blobs, and the cost of publication.
